abstract: Multi-Task Learning (MTL) enables a single model to learn multiple tasks simultaneously, leveraging knowledge transfer among tasks for enhanced generalization, and has been widely applied across various domains. However, task imbalance remains a major challenge in MTL. Although balancing the convergence speeds of different tasks is an effective approach to address this issue, it is highly challenging to accurately characterize the training dynamics and convergence speeds of multiple tasks within the complex MTL system. To this end, we attempt to analyze the training dynamics in MTL by leveraging Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) theory and propose a new MTL method, NTKMTL. Specifically, we introduce an extended NTK matrix for MTL and adopt spectral analysis to balance the convergence speeds of multiple tasks, thereby mitigating task imbalance. Based on the approximation via shared representation, we further propose NTKMTL-SR, achieving training efficiency while maintaining competitive performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our methods achieve state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of benchmarks, including both multi-task supervised learning and multi-task reinforcement learning. Source code is available at [https://github.com/jianke0604/NTKMTL](https://github.com/jianke0604/NTKMTL "").

bibliographic.title: NTKMTL: Mitigating Task Imbalance in Multi-Task Learning from Neural Tangent Kernel Perspective
bibliographic.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025)

content.problem: Task imbalance in multi-task learning, where some tasks dominate training while others are under-optimized, persists because accurately characterizing the training dynamics and convergence speeds of multiple tasks within a complex MTL system is very difficult, and prior loss-scale-based approximations fail to capture true convergence behavior.
content.proposed_solution: The authors extend Neural Tangent Kernel theory to MTL by introducing an extended NTK matrix whose spectral analysis reveals task-level convergence speeds, and propose NTKMTL, which normalizes the maximum eigenvalues of per-task NTK matrices to set task weights, plus an efficient shared-representation approximation NTKMTL-SR.

content.claim: By using NTK spectral analysis to balance per-task convergence speeds, NTKMTL and NTKMTL-SR achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance across supervised benchmarks with 2 to 40 tasks and multi-task reinforcement learning, with NTKMTL obtaining the best performance drop on NYUv2, CityScapes, and CelebA.
author_stated_limitations: The weight design of the current method only analyzes the task-specific diagonal NTK matrices rather than exploiting the full structure of the extended NTK matrix.
